# Packages this project declares, one name per line, consumed by
# lfreleng-actions/grype-scan-action as `declared-dependencies`.
#
# Why this file exists at all: the action would rather read the
# dependency graph out of our CycloneDX SBOM, but cyclonedx-py runs
# in environment mode here and so emits no `metadata.component`
# root. The action refuses an unrooted graph, and an unusable source
# leaves every finding classified as declared, which gates on
# exactly the inherited packages we cannot fix. This list is the
# documented fallback.
#
# The list MUST be complete with respect to pyproject.toml: anything
# missing from it is classified as inherited and is therefore gated
# more leniently. Add an entry here whenever a dependency is added to
# pyproject.toml, in the same spelling the SBOM uses for it. The one
# deliberate exception is recorded at the bottom of this file.
#
# Names, not purls, deliberately. A purl carries the resolved version,
# so a purl entry would stop matching the moment the version moved
# and would silently downgrade the package to inherited.

# The integration itself, as it appears in the SBOM.
homeassistant-hospitable

# [project] dependencies, shipped to users.
httpx
voluptuous

# [project.optional-dependencies] test and [dependency-groups] dev
# and releasenotes. Not shipped, but we do choose these versions, so
# a finding in one of them is ours to act on.
homeassistant
interrogate
mypy
pytest
pytest-asyncio
pytest-cov
pytest-homeassistant-custom-component
reno
respx
ruff

# [build-system] requires.
hatch-vcs
hatchling

# DELIBERATELY OMITTED: pillow.
#
# pyproject.toml declares "pillow>=11" in the test extra and the dev
# group, but only so the brand asset tests can import it by name
# rather than lean on Home Assistant pulling it in. We do not choose
# its version: Home Assistant pins pillow exactly, and our ">=11"
# floor always resolves to that pin. A finding in it therefore has no
# fix we can reach until Home Assistant moves its pin, which is the
# definition of an inherited package. Listing it would gate on every
# advisory against Home Assistant's pillow, the very unactionable red
# check this policy exists to remove.
#
# Revisit when pyproject.toml's pillow requirement starts to pin or
# cap the version itself, or if non-test code starts importing it.
